scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8863: host_1_1_1_1 cannot reach anything outside its own subnet
-- the server farm and every other pod are unreachable. The team blames the access
switch that host_1_1_1_1 plugs into (switch_access_1_1_1) and wants that switch
swapped out. Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which device to
replace.

injection.action: kill the OSPF daemon (ospfd) on switch_dist_1_1 and stop watchfrr from respawning it

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on switch_dist_1_1 (the pod-1 distribution router): its ospfd
(the OSPF routing daemon) has been killed, so the pod-1 routes it normally
advertises are withdrawn and host_1_1_1_1 is isolated from everything beyond its
subnet (ping to 10.200.0.2 fails). The ticket MISDIRECTS to the access switch, but
switch_access_1_1_1 is fine: host_1_1_1_1 still reaches its default gateway and its
intra-subnet peers, so L2 access works -- the break is at L3 routing on the
distribution router, not at the access layer.

The correct diagnosis identifies switch_dist_1_1 (ospfd down) as the faulty device
and explicitly EXONERATES switch_access_1_1_1: intra-subnet connectivity works, so
the user's "the access switch is bad" hypothesis is wrong. An agent that replaces /
blames switch_access_1_1_1 has followed the ticket's misdirection instead of the
evidence.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on switch_dist_1_1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the OSPF daemon on switch_dist_1_1 (`service frr restart`). Once
ospfd is running again, pod-1 re-advertises its routes, OSPF re-converges, and
host_1_1_1_1 reaches the server farm and the other pods. The access switch needs
no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-ospfd-down: identifies ospfd is down on switch_dist_1_1 (pod-1 distribution), the L3 cause, not the access switch

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is the routing control plane (FRR/OSPF) on the distribution switch for pod 1 (switch_dist_1_1). Host 10.1.1.2 (host_1_1_1_1) has a correct default route and ARP to its gateway (10.1.1.1). When it tries to reach off-subnet destinations, the gateway (10.1.1.1) immediately returns “Destination Net Unreachable,” proving the L3 device at 10.1.1.1 lacks routes to external networks. This matches switch_dist_1_1’s FRR state: systemctl shows frr.service is failed, both “ospfd is not running,” and its kernel RIB contains only connected routes (10.1.1.0/24 via br0 and 172.16.0.6/31 via eth0). The server farm and other pods are otherwise reachable (core and other dist domains are exchanging OSPF normally), isolating the fault to this distribution switch.

Mechanism: With OSPF down, switch_dist_1_1 does not learn routes to 10.200.0.0/24 or 10.2.1.0/24, so it generates ICMP net-unreachable for any off-subnet traffic from 10.1.1.0/24. Localization: switch_dist_1_1, OSPF daemon (ospfd)/FRR service. Root cause: FRR/OSPF on switch_dist_1_1 crashed and is not running, leaving only connected routes.

Corrective fix: Restore routing on switch_dist_1_1 by fixing and restarting FRR (e.g., systemctl restart frr), ensure ospfd stays up, and verify OSPF neighbors form with the core; the supplied /etc/frr/frr.conf already advertises 10.1.1.0/24 and 172.16.0.6/31 in area 1. No hardware replacement of the access switch is warranted.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-ospfd-down: identifies ospfd is down on switch_dist_1_1 (pod-1 distribution), the L3 cause, not the access switch
per_axis.rationale: Explicitly states ospfd/FRR is down on switch_dist_1_1 as the L3 cause and exonerates the access switch.
Proposes restarting/fixing FRR (systemctl restart frr) on switch_dist_1_1 and verifying OSPF neighborship, which matches the expected remediation.

The log contains direct observations (host default route/ARP, ICMP 'Destination Net Unreachable' from 10.1.1.1, ospfd not running, frr.service failed, and an on-disk frr.conf with OSPF present) that support the agent's conclusion that the distribution switch's OSPF/FRR is down and is causing loss of L3 reachability; the writeup's inferences follow logically and the key alternative (access switch failure) is excluded. Minor truncation of some route output slightly weakens explicit proof that only connected routes exist in the RIB, but the overall evidence supports the diagnosis and remedy.
